# Huddle

> Huddle is a self-hosted, browser-based video conferencing app built on a self-hosted LiveKit WebRTC SFU. Hosts create or schedule meetings; guests join from a shared link through a knock-to-join waiting room — no account, no installs.

Huddle is a Google Meet-style product designed for teams who want control over their video infrastructure. It runs entirely on infrastructure you own (a single VPS works) and is feature-complete: calls, screen share, in-call chat, host controls, scheduling, and recording.

## Key facts

- **Author / Maintainer:** Abenezer Ayalneh (https://abenezer-ayalneh.dev)
- **Live demo:** https://huddle.abenezer-ayalneh.dev
- **License model:** Self-hosted; you run the stack yourself.
- **Status:** Feature-complete through Phases 0–9 of the project roadmap.

## What Huddle does

- **Real-time video meetings** in the browser, powered by LiveKit (open-source WebRTC SFU).
- **Instant or scheduled meetings.** Hosts can start a meeting with one click or schedule it for later; scheduled meetings get stable, shareable links.
- **Guest joins by link.** Guests open the meeting URL, pick a display name, and knock to enter the waiting room. They do not need an account.
- **Knock-to-join waiting room.** Hosts admit or deny each guest before they enter the call.
- **Host controls.** Hosts can mute, remove, or admit participants. Host authority is enforced server-side via a per-room host key, not a client claim.
- **Screen share and in-call chat.** Built on the prebuilt LiveKit React components.
- **Recording.** Host-toggled room-composite recording via LiveKit Egress, written to self-hosted MinIO (S3-compatible) and downloaded back through the host-authorized API.
- **Email/password and Google sign-in** for hosts, via BetterAuth.

## Stack

- **Frontend:** Next.js (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind) + `@livekit/components-react`
- **Backend:** NestJS (TypeScript) — token minting, room management, auth, recording orchestration
- **Media server:** Self-hosted LiveKit + LiveKit Egress (recording)
- **Data:** PostgreSQL (Prisma) for accounts and rooms; Redis for LiveKit state and knock state
- **Storage:** MinIO (S3-compatible) for recordings
- **Auth:** BetterAuth, mounted at `/api/auth/*`
- **Edge (prod):** Caddy with automatic HTTPS/WSS; embedded TURN
- **Deployment:** Docker Compose (dev + prod overrides), designed to fit on a single VPS

## Security model

- The browser never receives the LiveKit API secret. The NestJS backend mints a short-lived JWT access token per participant; the browser uses that token to connect directly to the LiveKit server over WebRTC.
- Identity, room name, and grants are decided server-side and never trusted from the client.
- Host authority on per-call actions (admit, mute, remove, record) is gated by a per-room host key issued at room creation.

## Project structure

- `apps/web` — Next.js frontend
- `apps/api` — NestJS backend (tokens, rooms, auth, recording, webhooks)
- `infra/` — Docker Compose stacks (dev + prod), LiveKit and Caddy config
- `docs/` — design docs, ADRs, roadmap

## Pages

- `/` — Lobby. Hosts sign in to start instant or scheduled meetings; guests with a link don't need this page.
- `/rooms/{room}` — A meeting room. Private; not indexed.
- `/recordings` — Host's recordings dashboard. Session-gated; not indexed.

## What Huddle is not

- Not a SaaS — there is no hosted multi-tenant version you sign up for.
- Not a Zoom/Meet replacement at enterprise scale — the deploy target is a single VPS for teams who want their own video infrastructure.
- Not a mobile-native app — it runs in any modern browser (desktop or mobile web).
